# Prompt

> write more gates and test the gates.  Make sure the gates are all wired in.
> /ropensci-skills:run-performance-review

# Skill

`ropensci-skills:run-performance-review`, from
`~/.claude/plugins/cache/ropensci-skills/ropensci-skills/1.0.0/skills/run-performance-review`.
Its operative instructions, verbatim:

> - **Trace before you profile.** Understand the data/compute path end to end —
>   where I/O happens, where results accumulate — before quoting numbers.
> - **Anchor on measured data.** Profile real inputs, or measure the package's own
>   recorded fixtures (`object.size()`, row/column counts, per-row cost). State
>   which figures are _measured_ and which are _extrapolated_.
> - **Extrapolate explicitly.** Show the multipliers (rows/site/year, bytes/row,
>   transient vs. persistent) so a reader can check the arithmetic and see the
>   assumptions.
> - **Distinguish the persistent result from the transient peak** — the peak
>   (in-flight parse + accumulated result + concatenation copy) is usually what
>   OOMs, not the final object.
> - **Measured wins only.** Recommend an optimization only where the trace or a
>   measurement shows it matters; keep behaviour identical.
> - **Read-only.** Don't edit the package; propose, with evidence.

Report structure follows the shared template at
`../run-package-review/references/report-template.md`.

One deviation from the skill, stated up front: this repository is **not an R
package** — it is a pipeline of numbered and named scripts with no `DESCRIPTION`
and no namespace, so `devtools::load_all()` and per-export profiling do not
apply. Hot paths were traced through the scripts and the shared helpers in
`R/lib/` instead.

# Report

## Method

Everything below ran on one machine, stated because the memory findings depend
on it:

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | macOS 24.3.0 (darwin), 8 cores, **8.0 GB RAM** |
| R | 4.5.2 (2025-10-31) |
| Packages | readr 2.2.0 · dplyr 1.2.1 · duckdb 1.5.5 · arrow 25.0.1 · data.table 1.18.6.1 |
| Tree | `origin/main` at `bbba062`; findings re-verified against that commit's line numbers |

Measurement harness, all scripts kept in the session scratchpad, none of them in
the repository:

- Each timing arm ran in its **own `Rscript --vanilla` process**, so a peak is
  that arm's peak and not the previous arm's garbage.
- Peak memory is the OS figure — `/usr/bin/time -l`'s *maximum resident set
  size* — not `gc()`'s accounting. An earlier pass of this review used `gc()`
  and mis-scaled the Ncells/Vcells byte widths; every memory number in this
  report is RSS.
- readr 2.x returns lazy ALTREP columns, so a read timed without touching the
  data measures *not having read the file*. Every readr arm forces
  materialisation (`sum(nchar(as.character(col)))` over every column) inside the
  timed region.
- Row-level equivalence between a current implementation and its proposed
  replacement was checked with `identical()` on the full result, not on a
  sample.

**No repository files were modified for the measurements.** The gate added
alongside this report is separate work, requested in the same message, and is
additive (`tests/ci_read_width.R` and its detector); it changes no analysis
script.

## Headline

**Amber, and the colour is about time rather than memory.**

The architecture is already right where the data is biggest: every raw federal
extract — including a 963 MB CMS Physician Compare release — is read through
DuckDB with predicate and projection pushdown, and the 544 MB person-level panel
is *written* incrementally, one snapshot year at a time, so the producer never
holds it all. Nothing in the repository accumulates a frame quadratically, and
no per-row loop touches person-level data.

The cost is concentrated in one habit: **the derived panel is read full-width
at 28 sites across 24 files, and narrowed with `col_select` at exactly one**,
even though most of those sites reduce to three columns in the next statement.
Measured, with the answer proven byte-identical: the full-width read costs
**60.8 s** against **12.1 s** for the three columns actually used. Fourteen of
the twenty-four reader scripts are in `rebuild_frozen_dependents.R`'s plan, and
two of them read the panel three times each, so a full rebuild pays that penalty
**18 times** — an extrapolated **18.2 minutes** of pure re-parsing.

Worse per statement, and the single clearest win: `build_midwife_panel.R` spends
**210.9 s** at the end of a streamed build reading its own 544 MB output back
into base R to print four summary numbers. One DuckDB query — on a connection
the script already has open — returns the same four numbers in **6.7 s**. That
is **31×**, with identical output.

Memory is *not* the problem, and the obvious-sounding claim about it is false:
`col_select` does **not** reduce peak RSS (1,197 MB vs 1,186 MB — the file scan
dominates, not the retained columns). Peak RSS never exceeded **1.4 GB** in any
arm, comfortable even on this 8 GB laptop. CI is unaffected throughout: the
panel is gitignored (`.gitignore:61`), so no runner ever reads it. Every figure
here is a cost paid on a developer's machine.

## Measured anchors

The central artifact, `midwife_panel.csv` (gitignored; produced by
`build_midwife_panel.R`):

| property | value |
|---|---|
| bytes on disk | 544,742,809 (519.5 MB) |
| rows × columns | 4,735,546 × 13 |
| bytes/row on disk | 115 |
| distinct NPIs | 472,327 |
| distinct (NPI, surname) pairs | 507,559 |
| NPIs under more than one surname | 33,657 |

### Reading it (all measured, one process per arm)

| arm | elapsed | persistent `object.size()` | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read_csv(cols(.default = "c"))` — 13 cols, as written at 28 sites | **60.8 s** | 534.1 MB | 1,186 MB |
| `read_csv(col_select = 3 cols)` — as written at 1 site | **12.1 s** | 137.2 MB | 1,197 MB |
| `read_csv(cols(<10 × col_skip>))` — the `source_coverage.R` idiom | 12.4 s | 137.2 MB | 1,172 MB |
| `read.csv(colClasses = "character")` — base R, as written at 2 sites | 72.5 s | 534.0 MB | — |
| DuckDB `read_csv_auto` + `GROUP BY snapshot_year` | **4.4 s** | ~0 | 313 MB |

Two results worth stating because they contradict the intuitive version:

1. **Narrowing the read saves time, not memory.** 60.8 s → 12.1 s is a 5.0×
   speed-up, but peak RSS is unchanged (1,186 → 1,197 MB). readr streams all
   544 MB through its parse buffer whichever columns it keeps; the retained
   frame (534 → 137 MB) is a minority of the peak. Any recommendation below is
   a *latency* recommendation.
2. **`col_select` beats the `col_skip` column spec** (12.1 s vs 12.4 s) and is
   one argument instead of a constructed `cols()` object — relevant because
   `R/lib/source_coverage.R:330-336` builds the `col_skip` spec by hand.

### The summary tail of `build_midwife_panel.R` (lines 520–528)

Both arms produce the same four numbers, which is the point:

| step | as written (base R) | one DuckDB query |
|---|---|---|
| `read.csv(out_path, colClasses = "character")` | 72.5 s | — |
| `length(unique(npi))` + `nrow(unique(npi, last_name))` | 41.6 s | — |
| `aggregate(last_name ~ npi, panel, function(x) length(unique(x)))` | **96.8 s** | — |
| **total** | **210.9 s** | **6.7 s** |
| peak RSS | 1,169 MB | 593 MB |
| answers | 4735546 / 472327 / 507559 / 33657 | identical |

`build_truth_fusion_predictions.R:69-71`, reproduced verbatim (its own

|---|---|---|---|
| as written — full 13-column read | **125.6 s** | 4,728,364 | — |
| `col_select = c("npi", "snapshot_year", "practice_state")` | **52.8 s** | 4,728,364 | `identical() == TRUE` |

Peak RSS 1,333 MB for the process holding both.

### The shared reduction those sites recompute

| property | value |
|---|---|
| DuckDB build of `DISTINCT (npi, year, state)` | 25.0 s, peak RSS 419 MB |
| rows | 4,735,546 (every row is already a distinct triple) |

## What scales, and what does not

**Does not scale with the data** (so: leave alone):

- The CI gate suite. `tests/ci_hygiene.R` walks all 664 tracked R files for
  18.5 s of CPU; parsing the whole tree costs 5.3 s with source refs and 4.0 s
  without, and reading every file with `readLines()` costs 0.53 s — so the fact
  that each file is opened four times across H1/H2/H4/H6 is worth nothing to
  fix. (Wall-clock on this laptop was 48.6 s against 18.5 s of CPU; that gap is
  memory pressure from the measurements above, not the gate, and is not a
  finding.)
- `safe_left_join()` runs an extra full `anti_join()` on every call
  (`R/join_safety.R:683`) purely to count unmatched left rows, roughly doubling
  the join. All 15 non-test call sites are in `R/01-build-county-base.R`
  joining ~3,143-row county frames. A 2× cost on 3,143 rows is free; this is
  deliberately **not** a finding.
- Per-row `for` loops: 50 sites, every one of them over a manifest, summary
  table, or bounded work queue. None iterates person-level data.
- `stats::aggregate()`: 6 sites, five over frames of tens to hundreds of rows.

**Scales with the panel** (4.7 M rows, and growing by one snapshot year per
NPPES release — ~250 k rows/year, ~29 MB/year):

- the 23 full-width reads;
- `build_midwife_panel.R`'s summary tail, which grows in both the read (linear)
  and the `aggregate()` (linear in rows, with per-group R closure calls — 472 k
  groups today).

## Extrapolated scenarios

Estimates, from the measured per-read anchors. The multiplier is counted, not
guessed: 14 of the 24 panel-reading scripts appear by name in
`rebuild_frozen_dependents.R`'s plan, and within those,
`remake_oig_07_09_00440_midwifery.R` reads the panel at lines 253, 1137 and 1798
and `run_no_gold_standard_toolkit_on_real_data.R` at lines 91, 319 and 460 —
14 scripts, 18 reads.

| scenario | panel reads | time in `read_csv` | vs. narrowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| one analysis script, today | 1 | 60.8 s | 12.1 s |
| `remake_oig_07_09_00440_midwifery.R` alone | 3 | 182 s | 36 s |
| `REBUILD_APPLY=1 rebuild_frozen_dependents.R` | **18** | **1,094 s (18.2 min)** | **218 s (3.6 min)** |
| rebuild after 4 more NPPES releases (+1 M rows, +115 MB) | 18 | ~1,325 s (22.1 min) | ~264 s (4.4 min) |

The last row assumes cost is linear in rows, which the 115 bytes/row figure and
readr's streaming parse support but which was not measured at a second size.

## Findings

### Hot-path cost

**F1 — `build_midwife_panel.R:520-528` reads its own 544 MB output back into
base R to print four numbers. _(High.)_**

The script is otherwise exemplary: it writes the panel incrementally with
`write.table(..., append = !first)` per snapshot year (lines 370, 389, 501), so
it never holds more than one year. Line 520 then undoes that:

```r
panel <- read.csv(out_path, colClasses = "character")          # 72.5 s
cat(sprintf("\npanel: %s rows, %s distinct NPIs, %s distinct (NPI, surname) pairs\n",
            format(nrow(panel), big.mark = ","),
            format(length(unique(panel$npi)), big.mark = ","),
            format(nrow(unique(panel[, c("npi", "last_name")])), big.mark = ",")))  # 41.6 s
changed <- aggregate(last_name ~ npi, panel, function(x) length(unique(x)))         # 96.8 s
```

Why it is wrong, rather than merely slow: `aggregate()`'s formula method calls
an R closure once per group, and there are 472,327 groups, so the slowest
statement in the repository exists only to produce one `cat()` line. And the
cheaper tool is not a new dependency — it is **already connected in this
script** at line 317 (`con <- duckdb_connect()`), and `duckdb` is attached at
line 27.

Measured replacement, same four numbers (`4735546 / 472327 / 507559 / 33657`),
210.9 s → 6.7 s, peak RSS 1,169 → 593 MB:

```r
summary_row <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf("
  WITH p AS (SELECT npi, last_name FROM read_csv_auto('%s', all_varchar = TRUE))
  SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM p) AS rows,
         (SELECT count(DISTINCT npi) FROM p) AS npis,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT npi, last_name FROM p)) AS pairs,
         (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT npi FROM p GROUP BY npi
                                HAVING count(DISTINCT last_name) > 1)) AS multi_surname",
  out_path))
```

**F2 — 28 panel reads parse all 13 columns; 1 narrows. _(High.)_**

Counted by parse walk, not by grep. A line-oriented `git grep` for
`cols(.default = "c")` finds 23 reads in 19 files and **misses five**: the reads
that pass no column spec at all (`analyze_inclusive_zip_agreement.R:75`), the
ones that hide the spec behind a variable (`cc <- cols(.default = "c")` at
`analyze_consensus_tier_persistence_2021_2025.R:50`), and the ones that reach
the file through `Sys.getenv("MIDWIFE_PANEL", "midwife_panel.csv")`. The AST
figure is the one used throughout this report:

```
$ Rscript tests/ci_read_width.R
  ok   no NEW full-width read of midwife_panel.csv
       (28 grandfathered across 24 file(s) in tests/ci_read_width_baseline.txt)
$ git grep -n 'read_csv("midwife_panel.csv", col_select' -- '*.R'
compare_all_sources_mysteryroster.R:159
```

This is a reuse finding before it is a performance finding: the cheaper idiom is
already in the tree, written once, in a file that reads the same three columns
the others do.

Five scripts carry a **byte-identical** three-line reduction —
`audit_migration_corroboration_by_transition.R:97`,
`build_leave_one_source_out_sensitivity.R:50`,
`build_migration_rate_by_method.R:35`,
`build_truth_fusion_predictions.R:69`,
`diagnose_truth_fusion_migration_states.R:73`:

```r
nppes <- read_csv("midwife_panel.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"), progress = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(npi = trimws(npi), year = as.integer(snapshot_year), state = clean_state(practice_state)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(npi), nzchar(npi), !is.na(state), npi %in% link$npi) %>% distinct(npi, year, state)
```

Every one of the 13 columns is parsed; the next line keeps three.
`remake_oig_07_09_00440_midwifery.R:1137` and `:1798` are the same reduction with
different year windows, and `run_no_gold_standard_toolkit_on_real_data.R:319`
makes seven. `analyze_inclusive_zip_agreement.R:75` and
`analyze_medicaid_2023_2024_transition_support.R:64` are the same shape through
a different filter, for eight provable sites in all.

The fix is one argument, and it does not change the answer — proven above with
`identical() == TRUE` on all 4,728,364 rows:

```r
read_csv("midwife_panel.csv",
         col_select = c("npi", "snapshot_year", "practice_state"),
         col_types = cols(.default = "c"), progress = FALSE)
```

Calibration: most of the 28 sites reference four or fewer of the 13 column
names within the read's own pipeline, but that is a **floor**, not proof — a
site that only filters by `snapshot_year` may use wider columns later in the
script, and several genuinely do (the three address-comparison scripts need the
four `practice_*` columns; the two name-matching scripts need the three name
columns). `tests/ci_read_width_baseline.txt` records which of the 24 are
provable and which are wider, with a reason per file. Narrow the eight marked
PROVABLE first.

**F3 — seven sites recompute the same `(npi, year, state)` reduction from
scratch. _(Medium.)_**

The result is 85.8 MB on disk and takes 25.0 s to build once in DuckDB.
Materialising it as a provenance-stamped artifact turns 7 × 60.8 s of parsing
into 1 × 25.0 s plus seven small reads, and removes the duplication F2 only
narrows.

Stated as Medium and second to F2 deliberately: this adds an artifact, a
provenance sidecar, a staleness relationship and a line in the rebuild graph.
`col_select` adds nothing. Do F2 first and only reach for F3 if rebuild
wall-clock still matters.

### Silent failure paths

**F4 — DuckDB discards malformed rows and nothing counts them. _(Medium.)_**

`build_midwife_panel.R:411-413` reads every NPPES release with
`ignore_errors = true`:

```r
reader <- function(enc, ignore_errors = TRUE) sprintf(
  "read_csv_auto('%s', all_varchar = TRUE, sample_size = 1000,
                 normalize_names = TRUE, encoding = '%s', ignore_errors = %s)",
  f, enc, if (ignore_errors) "true" else "false")
```

The flag is deliberate and the comment above it is right about the dangerous
case (an encoding probe must *not* use it, or a wrong encoding silently drops
every row with a non-ASCII byte — lines 414-421). The residual risk is the one
the comment does not cover: for genuinely malformed rows, DuckDB drops them and
returns success, and the count printed at line 501 is the count of rows that
**passed the taxonomy filter**, so there is no number anywhere that would move
if a future release started emitting broken rows. A release that silently lost
10 % of its rows would look like a release with 10 % fewer midwives.

`store_rejects` / `rejects_table` is unused across the whole repository
(`git grep store_rejects` → nothing). Adding `store_rejects = true` to the full
read and refusing a non-zero reject count — or at minimum printing it beside the
row count — turns a silent loss into a visible one.

### Minor

**F5 — the resume path reads the whole output to learn which years are done.
_(Low.)_** `build_midwife_panel.R:353`:

```r
done_years <- unique(as.integer(read.csv(out_path, colClasses = "character")$snapshot_year))
```

72.5 s and 534 MB to answer `SELECT DISTINCT snapshot_year`, which the open
DuckDB connection answers in about a second. Low only because `RESUME` is not
the common path.

**F6 — `guess_max = Inf` with `.default = col_guess()` forces a full
type-inference pass. _(Low.)_** `build_results_geographic_persistence.R:67` and
`build_results_geographic_persistence_canonical.R:66`:

```r
panel <- read_csv(PANEL, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = Inf,
                  col_types = cols(practice_zip = "c", .default = col_guess()))
```

Because the spec is partial, readr must scan all 4,735,546 rows to guess the
other twelve types before parsing them. The panel's schema is fixed and known
(its producer writes 13 named columns), so naming the types removes the pass.
Note that `reconcile_linkage.R:32` uses `guess_max = Inf` **with a recorded
reason** (a column that is NA for most rows and a real 10-digit value late in
the file) — that one is correct and should stay.

## Verified healthy (no action)

- **DuckDB where the data is biggest, with pushdown.** The 963 MB
  `National_Downloadable_File_2013-06.csv` and its siblings, the 537 MB
  revalidation file, and the 132 MB facility-affiliation file are all read
  through `read_csv_auto` inside SQL that projects and filters before anything
  reaches R (`extract_physician_compare_historical_midwives.R:121`,
  `R/lib/match_npi_to_hospitals.R:201`, `build_midwife_panel.R:411`). Of the 15
  `SELECT *` occurrences outside tests, 13 are `LIMIT 0` header probes and one
  is a documented 50,000-row encoding probe.
- **The producer streams.** `build_midwife_panel.R` writes one snapshot year at
  a time (lines 370, 389, 501) and never holds the 4.7 M-row result — which is
  exactly what makes F1 stand out.
- **No quadratic accumulation.** No `x <- rbind(x, …)` or
  `x <- bind_rows(x, …)` inside a loop over data. The one self-accumulating
  `bind_rows` in a loop (`R/lib/source_coverage.R:646`) is bounded by the number
  of undeclared panel years — single digits, normally zero.
- **No per-row loop over person-level data.** All 50
  `for (i in seq_len(nrow(…)))` loops iterate manifests, summary tables or
  bounded queues.
- **Network paths are properly engineered.** `generate_osmde_isochrones.R:110-128`
  retries three times, honours the `retry-after` header, and backs off
  (`SLEEP_S * attempt * 2`); the per-location cache means an aborted run resumes
  for free. `scrape_healthgrades_midwives.R` and `scrape_doximity_public_cnm.R`
  checkpoint and resume, write atomically via `R/lib/resume_state.R`, and
  rate-limit. The checkpoint-interval trade-off at
  `scrape_healthgrades_midwives.R:59-73` is reasoned from a test
  (`tests/test_recovery_resume_equivalence.R` E4) and its residual torn-write
  risk is already logged in `DEBT.md` — correctly scoped, not re-raised here.
- **Repeated-read defects have already been found and fixed once.**
  `R/lib/source_coverage.R:415-429` describes each panel file **once** and looks
  the result up per declared row; the comment at lines 250-258 records the
  defect it replaced ("twenty full reads of a 700 MB CSV to answer twenty
  variants of one question"). That function also narrows its read to the
  declared columns (lines 330-336). F2 is the same lesson, not yet applied to the
  consumer scripts.
- **Type-inference cost was already measured in the right place.**
  `build_midwife_panel.R:400-410` records that `sample_size = -1` "forced a full
  multi-GB scan that failed outright on every release from 2018 onward" and that
  the encoding must be resolved per file. Both are correct.
- **Truncation in reporting is detected, not silent.** `R/join_safety.R:840-841`
  flags a truncated unmatched-key list and carries the pre-truncation count.
- **CI is not exposed to any of this.** `midwife_panel.csv` is gitignored
  (`.gitignore:61`) and named by no workflow step, so no runner reads it.
  `read_csv_auto` sites that would touch multi-GB inputs are likewise local-only.

## Not run (reason)

- **No end-to-end pipeline execution.** `rebuild_frozen_dependents.R` is dry-run
  by default and a real `REBUILD_APPLY=1` pass spans scrapers, paid geocoding
  and multi-hour DuckDB work. The 15.2-minute rebuild figure is an
  **extrapolation** from the measured 60.8 s single read times a counted
  multiplier, not a timed rebuild.
- **No second input size.** Scaling is assumed linear in rows from the 115
  bytes/row anchor and readr's streaming parse. Not measured at a second size,
  so the "+4 NPPES releases" row is the softest number in this report.
- **No CI-runner measurement.** Deliberate: the panel is gitignored, so runner
  figures would describe a path that does not execute there.
- **The 963 MB CMS Physician Compare path was traced, not timed.** It is already
  DuckDB-with-pushdown, so a measurement would have confirmed a design that the
  trace shows is correct; measuring it would have cost ~15 minutes per arm for
  no decision.
- **No `profmem`/allocation profiling.** `Rprof(line.profiling = TRUE)` over
  `tests/ci_hygiene.R` returned `<no location>` for 100 % of samples because the
  gate is `source()`d and exits via its own reporter; the per-arm process timings
  replaced it and were sufficient.
- **No change to any analysis script.** Read-only, per the skill.

## Suggested fix priority

1. **F1 _(High)_** — replace `build_midwife_panel.R:520-528` with the one
   DuckDB query on the already-open `con`. 210.9 s → 6.7 s, identical output,
   smallest diff of anything here.
2. **F2 _(High)_** — add `col_select` to the eight sites the baseline marks
   PROVABLE (`analyze_inclusive_zip_agreement.R:75`,
   `analyze_medicaid_2023_2024_transition_support.R:64`,
   `audit_migration_corroboration_by_transition.R:97`,
   `build_leave_one_source_out_sensitivity.R:50`,
   `build_migration_rate_by_method.R:35`,
   `build_truth_fusion_predictions.R:69`,
   `diagnose_truth_fusion_migration_states.R:73`, and
   `remake_oig_07_09_00440_midwifery.R:1137`/`:1798` plus
   `run_no_gold_standard_toolkit_on_real_data.R:319`). ~48.7 s each, answer
   proven identical. Then work outward through the rest by reading what each
   script actually uses.
3. **F4 _(Medium)_** — `store_rejects = true` on the full NPPES read, and refuse
   or at least print a non-zero reject count. This one is about trust in the
   data, not speed, and it is the only finding here that could be hiding a
   wrong number rather than a slow one.
4. **F5 _(Low)_** — `SELECT DISTINCT snapshot_year` in place of the full
   `read.csv` on the resume path (`build_midwife_panel.R:353`).
5. **F6 _(Low)_** — name the panel's column types at
   `build_results_geographic_persistence.R:67` and `_canonical.R:66` instead of
   `guess_max = Inf`. Leave `reconcile_linkage.R:32` alone.
6. **F3 _(Medium, but last)_** — materialise the shared `(npi, year, state)`
   artifact only if rebuild wall-clock still matters after F2. It buys less than
   F2 per unit of new machinery.

## Fixed (applied after the review, same branch)

The review above is read-only and was written against `bbba062`; the fixes
below were applied afterwards, each one re-measured rather than assumed. The
read-only claim in **Method** covers the measurements, not this section.

| finding | before | after | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** summary tail | 210.9 s, 1,169 MB peak | **6.7 s, 593 MB** | same four values: `4735546 / 472327 / 507559 / 33657` |
| **F2** 11 reads narrowed | 60.8 s each | **12.1 s each** | `identical()` per column set, over all 4,735,546 rows |
| **F4** reject accounting | nothing counted | per-release count printed | `store_rejects = true`, reject count reported |
| **F5** resume probe | 72.5 s, 534 MB held | **5.0 s, 217 MB peak** | same 20 snapshot years, 2007-2026 |
| **F6** type inference | 96.8 s | **43.0 s** | `identical()` on the whole 13-column frame |

**F2 in detail.** Eleven reads across nine files now name their columns, so the
baseline in `tests/ci_read_width_baseline.txt` went from 28 reads across 24
files to 17 across 17. Four distinct column sets were narrowed, and each was
checked by reading the file both ways in one process and comparing the narrowed
frame to the same columns of the full-width frame:

| `col_select` | sites | narrowed read | `identical()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c(npi, snapshot_year, practice_state)` | 7 | 9.5 s | TRUE |
| `c(npi, snapshot_year, practice_zip)` | 1 | 11.7 s | TRUE |
| `c(npi, snapshot_year, snapshot_date, practice_state)` | 1 | 29.1 s | TRUE |
| `c(npi, deactivation_date)` | 1 | 9.6 s | TRUE |

(The full-width read in that same process took 89.3 s rather than the 60.8 s of
the isolated arm — six reads of a 544 MB file in one R session pay for each
other's garbage collection. The isolated per-arm figures in **Measured anchors**
are the ones to quote; these four are for the comparison, which is what the
column proves.)

Eight of the seventeen remaining full-width reads are in
`rebuild_frozen_dependents.R`'s plan, so the extrapolated readr cost of one
`REBUILD_APPLY` pass over this file drops from **18.2 minutes to 8.1 minutes**.

**F6 is not a narrowing.** Both geographic-persistence scripts genuinely use
most of the panel, so they still read all thirteen columns — what was removed
is the *type-inference pass* that `guess_max = Inf` forced over all 4,735,546
rows because the spec was partial (`.default = col_guess()`). The replacement
names all thirteen types explicitly, and they are the types that scan arrives
at (`npi`, `snapshot_year` and `snapshot_date` as doubles, the other ten as
character) — verified by `identical()` on the whole frame, because getting
`npi`'s type wrong would silently break every downstream join against a
linkage file that is itself read with guessing on. `reconcile_linkage.R:32` was
left alone, as the finding said.

**F4 changes no number and adds one.** `store_rejects = true` is tied to
`ignore_errors` in `reader()` rather than set globally, because
`store_rejects` suppresses parse errors *by itself*: setting it on the strict
encoding probe would have defeated that probe exactly as `ignore_errors` would,
which is the trap the surrounding comment was already written about. The count
is a delta against `reject_errors`, taken *before* the `next` that skips a
release with zero usable rows — that release is precisely the case where the
reject count is the only thing left to report. Not measured on a full NPPES
release: the flag's cost on a multi-GB file is unknown, and the reject tables
were exercised on a four-row fixture instead.

**What the gate learned.** Narrowing the reads surfaced a third way this gate
had been reporting a smaller number than the truth: `panel_vars()` resolved
path variables with a single-line regex, so it could not see
`build_midwife_panel.R`'s `out_path`, which is assigned across five lines. The
two most expensive reads in the repository — F1 and F5, 283 s between them —
were therefore invisible to the gate that exists to find exactly them. It now
resolves assignments from the parse tree it was already walking, and
`tests/test_read_width_detect.R` RW10 plants a multi-line assignment back.

### Held closed

F2 is a habit, so narrowing eight call sites does not stop the twenty-ninth
from being written. `tests/ci_read_width.R` (added with this report) refuses a
**new** full-width read of the panel against a shrink-only baseline — 28 reads
when this report was written, 17 after the fixes above — keyed on the file and
a count rather than a line number so ordinary edits do not churn it.
`tests/test_read_width_detect.R` plants the defect back in eleven cases --
including all three ways this gate silently under-reported while it was being
written: a path arriving through a variable, a file listing that scanned
nothing, and a path assigned across more than one line — and requires the
gate to die on each.

Both ran green from the repository root and from inside `tests/`, and both are
named by the `r-checks` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, detector first.
